subtype: Approach: wait and see because it may not be serious [Pitfall]
passage: I'm Tanuja, and I live upstairs from Hrithik. Twice this monsoon the town had flood warnings, and twice the water stopped at the road. So on Monday, when the siren went again, I packed a bag and knocked on Hrithik's door. "Same as last time, it'll pass," Hrithik said, and turned the television up. By evening the drain outside was gurgling. At nine the water was over the doorstep, and by ten the lane to the main road had vanished under brown water and nobody could leave. Hrithik carried a suitcase up to my flat and stood on the stairs with a phone in hand, saying nothing. Downstairs the mattress and books were already soaked and the power was out. I felt sick watching the water climb. I don't know what was in Hrithik's mind. I only know the earlier warnings had been harmless.

qa.q: At what time was the water over the doorstep?
qa.a: At nine the water was over the doorstep.

qa.q: What might Hrithik have been thinking when saying it would pass?
qa.a: Hrithik probably felt calm and a little dismissive, since earlier warnings passed with little harm, though Tanuja can only guess.

qa.q: What could Hrithik have done differently, and why?
qa.a: Hrithik could have left with Tanuja when the siren first went, because a warning that ended harmlessly before does not mean the next will, and routes get cut once the water rises.

qa.q: What was it like for Tanuja to watch Hrithik stay behind?
qa.a: Tanuja felt worried and helpless, sick as the water climbed while Hrithik stayed put.

grounding: Illustrates staying put because earlier warnings passed harmlessly and leaving only after water enters the ground floor and routes are cut.
